best_echo_sets.commentary: Offers a 10% unconditional Healing% boost and an most importantly a 15% ATK% boost for the entire team, lasting 30 seconds whenever you heal yourself or any of your allies. This bonus can be triggered by character abilities and weapon effects, is easy to keep active 100% of the time and is a big help for all party members.

main_echo_options.echo_commentary: Grants 10% increased Energy Regeneration for the wearer and a team wide 10% ATK boost on use for 20 seconds. A strong option for those looking to generate as much energy as possible or who favor a more permanent party buffing effect compared to Bell-Borne Geochelone.

While nowadays a worse option for the Rejuvenating Glow set for damage than the Fallacy of No Return due to a shorter buff uptime, only granting 10% DMG Bonus for 15 seconds, the Bell-Borne Geochelone remains a good choice if you don't have a good Fallacy to use for the set. It also has increased survivability by blocking 50% of the damage from a max of 3 hits if you desire to have that in your team.

best_weapons.commentary_details: The best overall weapon for all Rectifier damage dealers. While Buling is not a damage-oriented character being mostly a Support, she does want to optimize her damage ideally since none of her buffs scale off of a particular stat or condition. As Stringmaster is the best general option for Rectifier damage dealers, it is also the strongest option on Buling thanks to its huge universal damage buffs.

best_weapons.commentary_details: As another strong generalist option, Phrolova's Signature enables Buling to deal a good chunk of damage while not packing as much of a punch as Stringmaster, making it the second best option available for her.

best_weapons.commentary_details: Mostly an ATK and CRIT DMG stat-stick for Buling, who can barely stack its Basic Attack DMG-oriented effect, but it can still be used decently on her.

When casting Outro Skill with 3 stacks, consume all stacks to give {1} DMG Bonus to the off-field Basic Attacks performed by the equipped Resonator, lasting for 27s.

best_weapons.commentary_details: Simple ATK and CRIT Rate stat-stick for Buling, who does not benefit from this weapon's Spectro Frazzle-oriented effects.

Dealing DMG to targets with Spectro Frazzle grants the wielder {1} Basic Attack DMG Bonus and {1} Heavy Attack DMG Bonus, stacking up to 3 times for 6s. Casting Outro Skill Amplifies the Spectro Frazzle DMG on targets around the active Resonator by {2} for 30s. Effects of the same name cannot be stacked.

best_weapons.commentary_details: Strongest permanently available option, which grants a lot of ATK and increased Energy Regen as well as some minor amounts of Basic Attack DMG to the wearer which Buling uses decently. One of the strongest options to increase Buling's Healing capabilities while simultaneously increasing her damage by a solid amount, this option can be considered even over above options in order to optimize Buling's Sustain capabilities.

weapon_base_info.effect_description: Increases Energy Regen by {0}. When hitting a target with Basic Attacks, increases Basic Attack DMG Bonus by {1}, stacking up to {2} time(s). This effect lasts for {3}s and can be triggered 1 time(s) every 0.5s.

best_weapons.commentary_details: Fully F2P-accessible craftable weapon that capitalizes on Buling's ability to instantly apply Electro Flare on her enemies, which allows this weapon's ATK-increasing passive to be quickly stacked up to the maximum effect for a lot of ATK buffing in total. Still pales in comparison to any 5-stars due to a lack of solid Base ATK.

weapon_base_info.effect_description: Dealing DMG to enemies with Negative Statuses increases the wielder's ATK by {0} for 10s. This effect can be triggered 1 time per second, stackable up to 4 times.

cons: Almost always worse than Verina as a generalist. For endgame-level accounts who already own specialized Supports for specialized teams (different forms of Rover, Chisa, Lupa etc.) as well as Shorekeeper, she may never see use;
A lot of her general buffing potential is tied to Skill damage dealers, which limits teams where she stands out, as well as her S6, which is not easily accessible in the short-term;

Lacks a Death Resist ability like Baizhi at S5, or Shorekeeper and Verina's second passives. Other Supports will be favoured if players want this kind of survivability perk on their team (however, this is optional and doesn't hinder team damage).
pros: Good generalist buffing reminiscent of already known viable Supports like Verina and Baizhi, featuring her own constant off-field healing while being able to inflict Electro Flare on enemies (may be relevant for future use cases);
Needs close to no investment whatsoever to perform;
As a 4-star character, it is quite easy to access permanently alongside Sequence nodes;
Basically always better than Baizhi. A new 4-star release that has a solid use case for once!

sections.heading: Summary
paragraphs: Buling is a 4-star Electro Rectifier Support character with abilities ranging from healing, to Electro Flare/Rage application, to general and specialized buffs oriented towards Skill damage dealers. Specialized in buffing Skill damage Main DPS characters like Carlotta and Phrolova, while retaining more generically applicable buffs for account-wide use, Buling is a character with easy gameplay yet pretty viable buffs that are definitely worth checking out.

sections.heading: Key Mechanics & Buffs
paragraphs: Buling's kit allows her to provide the team with the following array of buffs & utilities when fully executing her rotation:
10% team-wide Skill DMG Bonus for 24s after casting her Enhanced Ultimate and any character's Intro, which can go up to 25% when a Second Intro is cast (goes up to 50% at S6);
15% team-wide General DMG Amplification for 30s when casting her Outro (doesn't expire when swapping);
25% team-wide ATK for 20s with the Rejuvenating Glow Echo set and Fallacy of No Return (which she should always run in her current teams);
Healing on her Intro, some of her Heavy Attacks and her Outro (constant off-field healing to the active character);

Periodic Electro Flare application via her Intro and enhanced Ultimate (turns into Electro Rage at 10 stacks or above - deals periodic damage to afflicted enemies, possibly enhanced if Electro Rage is also applied up to 10 stacks);
Small amounts of enemy grouping via her Skill.

As can be seen above, a lot of her kit revolves around building up to an Enhanced Ultimate, and that is indeed the focus of her kit; obtained by activating 2 of her unique set of Heavy Attacks, Buling's gameplay revolves around generating and consuming at least 4 Trigrams in order to access her Enhanced Ultimate to apply the majority of her buffs to then end her rotation.

sections.heading: Moveset & Rotation
paragraphs: Aside from some specific Heavy Attacks, Buling will always use almost all of her moveset to execute her rotations so all of her available moves are worth using. They all revolve around accomplishing the goal of generating enough Trigrams to access her enhanced Ultimate.

Buling possesses several ways to generate Trigrams, including her Basic 2, Basic 4, Skill and Mid-Air Attack. We make use of all of these features in her rotation. She can generate Thunder Trigrams and Mountain Trigrams, the former being acquired via her Basic 4, Skill and Mid-Air Attack while the latter is only acquired via her Basic 2. This causes an imbalance of Trigrams and she will tend to generate many more Thunder than Mountain Trigrams. Different Heavy Attacks exist depending on the combinations of Trigrams, but in practice we will use the "Mountain over Thunder" and "Twin Thunders" attacks to execute our rotations (since they can be generated in this order the quickest).

To do so, we generate a Mountain and Thunder Trigram by executing a Basic Attack 2 into Basic Attack 4 (during the Opener, to generate extra Concerto Energy) or Mid-Air Attack (during her loop rotation, since her Intro gives the Concerto needed), then we can use her Skill which directly combos into her Basic 4 for 2 quick extra Thunder Trigrams. Since we're holding the max of 4 Trigrams, we can then cast her Heavy Attacks to access our Enhanced Ultimate and finish her rotation.

Buling's Dodge Counter also allows her to directly transition into her Basic Attack 3, which means it's perfectly usable to follow with the rest of your rotation if necessary. Even if no Mountain Trigrams end up being generated, there's no need to worry; all Heavy Attacks give the same amount of Concerto Energy and the rotation will work fine.

sections.heading: Meta Position & Conclusion
paragraphs: Overall, Buling is a 4-star Support that unfortunately won't have a position on the teams of most endgame accounts. While she is a solid universal Support, and she at least stands out from Baizhi in this role often providing more personal damage and a more consistent rotation with very similar general buffs, yet stronger specialized buffs, Buling does not provide more utility than any other dedicated Support or general 5-star Support like Shorekeeper and Verina do to begin with. Verina's rotation being one of the shortest in the game while still providing close to the same buffing strength means that Buling's slightly higher personal damage (which is not particularly praise-worthy) does not allow her to stand out, even at S6. However, Buling does match Verina in some teams, being the Carlotta and Phrolova teams as they are both primarily Skill damage dealers. This enables Buling to buff those characters as well as Verina, albeit with slightly increased rotation time (again, only at S6).

While Buling's buffing profile is theoretically universally strong for all Skill damage dealers, a lot of her buffing utility (25% Skill DMG Bonus) is locked behind her S6, on top of having very high Energy requirements before her S2 (which makes optimizing her for damage below that threshold much harder). In terms of general use cases, Buling is not comparable to Verina and suffers a lot of comparison from the easy to access Spectro 5-star generalist that can slot into pretty much any team effectively. Buling also sees very little use in teams with certain Skill damage dealers like Jinhsi since she lacks the Coordinated Attacks required to make Jinhsi generate her Forte stacks that enable her damage, which makes her suffer from an even bigger gap in team damage with a support like Verina, whether Buling's S6 is factored in or not.

In conclusion, Buling is a viable generalist 4-star Support, she suffers from comparisons with the previously generally strong 5-star Supports and other dedicated team Supports like Spectro and Aero Rover which serve unique roles in their teams that Buling cannot fulfill. While this means Buling can very much be considered an alternative Support choice in several teams (particularly Skill damage-focused ones) and can allow newer accounts to compose teams with a multitude of generalist Supports for endgame contents, in the meta Buling will lack a spot on a lot of endgame accounts as she doesn't stand out enough in any single given team. However, she can very much be considered if you need one extra Support for your endgame teams!

synergies.commentary: Buling's best DPS characters to buff as they are Main Skill DMG-oriented DPS. Thanks to Buling's Outro, Echo Set and passive (enhanced via S6), she is capable of providing them with a wide array of ATK, DMG Amplification and Skill DMG Bonus buffs, which makes her suited as a solid Support choice for those teams, particularly if her S6 is unlocked.
